title: Procedure lives in skills, not in agent bodies or always-on rules
context: An agent body is paid for on every dispatch whether relevant or not, and the always-on rules are sent verbatim to every cold subagent — verified by a probe agent that quoted all 18 rules/common files back without using a single tool, at a cost of 51,740 bytes per dispatch. A skill's description is always in context but its body loads only on invocation, and a skill travels into a fork for free because a fork inherits the conversation. Two of the thirteen agents (conformance-auditor, platform-engineer) duplicated skills of the same name that already existed.
options: Keep procedure in agent bodies where it is today
Duplicate procedure across both agent bodies and skills
Move procedure into skills and preload it into agents with the skills: frontmatter field
outcome: Procedure moves to skills. Retained agents carry role, entry invariant, output format and stop conditions only, pulling procedure via the skills: frontmatter field, which injects full skill content at startup. Four new skills are created from surviving procedure (writing-tests, committing-work, reviewing-code, research-citations); five deleted agents produce no skill at all because their content was persona or duplication. Five always-on rule files move into skills and seven are deleted outright, cutting the preamble from about 12,935 to about 2,520 tokens. Constraint recorded: a skill with disable-model-invocation true cannot be preloaded into a subagent, so any skill named in a skills: field must leave that flag unset — acceptance check 8.7.
